## Haskell fix handoff for external work

External Haskell documentation follow-up: 2026-10-20 14:55 CEST.
Source inspection found a possible overclaim in the new Typing.hs size-order
paragraph and cfta-generator README: "Binders generators already have
size-major ranks". fromTypingRules uses fromConstructorAutomaton, whose
route depends on actual graph cycles. An acyclic Binders grammar can use
finite constructor order. Candidate: Payload = P Payload | Z and T = A Payload | B Int, with only
rules A(value(P(P Z))) and B(value0), bound Binders0. Both roots have arity1.
The larger A term can precede the B term by finite constructor order. This
valid external-field candidate did not reach rank output in the isolated
cached-dependency reproduction. Seven capped attempts retained compiler and
linker failures; the final executable aborted with exit134 and
"*** stack smashing detected ***". No fresh package build was run. This is
a verification blocker, not evidence of a production runtime defect. Verify
the candidate with a fresh matching toolchain before requesting a repair.
If confirmed, qualify the statement
by the actual cyclic route and retain the upToSize advice for acyclic imports.
No production Haskell file is changed locally. Keep this follow-up separate
from confirmed runtime defects and from the older repair registry below.

# Structural rows from completed source builds

The proof checkpoint is `330e6fd55`. The verified start is `d7dc85792`.
Main remains `9769fe3e9`. The ff-only refresh imports no change.

`SourceCurrentBuildStructuralRowOrigins.build_row_origin` consumes an actual
completed FreshOrdinary build, its initial lexical Context and exact RowAt.
It derives `SourceRow`. The relation has four alternatives.

The node alternative retains the actual buildEdges and makeNode equations.
Its canonical output lookup selects the same complete row as its original
source RowCall. That RowCall retains the original EdgeSyntax, symbol, guard,
ordered child syntax and values, actual buildMany and makeEdge, source row
index, exact execution prefix and suffix, historical Context and growth.
The canonical output and original source indices have separate roles.
A repeated equal row can have several genuine source occurrences. The
statement selects one actual occurrence. It does not prove uniqueness.

The union alternative retains an actual buildMany and makeUnion. One index
selects the same original expression and returned value. The exact source
prefix, selected call and suffix remain explicit. The producer recurses on
that strictly smaller original member. Its normalization inversion retains
a literal ordinary row or an entire opaque Mu with the same internal row.
It does not unfold Mu during this step.

The capture alternative retains the exact source variable slot and returned
captured value. A missing slot returns Empty and cannot supply a row. The
statement does not supply the capture's original binding history.

The binder alternative retains both actual probe callbacks and the actual
request. It selects the exact Mu payload at the actual return heap and the
actual smart finish. This includes a warm winner whose body differs from
the current callback. Raw and smart-used binders expose a structural row
in that selected body. Smart-unused cleanup returns that same body.
Bare-self cleanup returns Empty and cannot supply a row. The selected
winner's original publication writer and source ancestry remain separate.

The induction uses strict original syntax size only for union members.
It supplies no global descent through capture or selected-winner arms.
The node child calls remain actual original calls; their descendants are
not recursively classified by this statement. No generated child bound,
original binding ancestry, global renewal, general active-owner exclusion,
outer completion, repeated-pass convergence or Haskell refinement is proved.
The conditional root-language theorem and Sized query contracts are unchanged.

Root personally observed strict1 with an empty log, canonical1 terminal0,
and Full1 with two complete public statements, proofs and standard-axiom
readbacks. All eight printer settings are present. The default Audit handle
13114 terminates0:3476jobs73986dependencies. Its sole warning is the existing
ClosedCompletion unused-input warning. Pinned Lean4.34.1 checks use the
4GiB hard/high memory cap, zero swap and a five-minute wall cap.

One constructed Nat/Bool theorem checks five actual call families. A seed
allocation makes source row1 become canonical row0 in rows [9,3,9]; two equal
source rows normalize to one row. A union selects an actual nonempty member.
A lexical var0 returns that actual available union result. A used Mu built
from node7[x] is then returned by a warm binder whose body syntax is
union[Empty,node7[x]]. The final case checks smart-unused ordinary cleanup.
Every case invokes the official producer from an actual derived Context.
The fixture supplies no desired row origin premise. It does not establish
writer uniqueness or different stored-body outputs for the two callback
syntaxes. It does not test bare-self Empty cleanup. Strict2 has an empty log;
Full1 checks one complete constructed declaration and standard axioms.
All three capped fixture attempts remain, including one elaboration failure.

The isolated prototype and all five attempts remain preserved. Its author
performed a separate full mathematical reread. This is not a second author
review. Root also read the entire final 315-line source. No Haskell build,
test, repair or local behavior edit is added. FINDINGS retains external
repairs first, including the earlier unvalidated Typing documentation candidate.
Read `restart-evidence/20261020-build-structural-row-origins/next-binding-ancestry-handoff.md`.
The whole-library goal is active. Publication to formalize is authorized.

In simple technical English: fresh construction always finishes in the
Lean model. Under the stated guard conditions, its result represents
exactly the finite trees specified by its expression. A completed supported
modeled root reduction with empty inherited constraints preserves that
exact language.
The root theorem derives the logical startup cache and guard facts.
Field allocation, validity, guard coverage and numeric resources remain
explicit. General termination and Haskell correspondence remain open.

Completed source builds now derive the exact row alternative from actual
calls. Ordinary rows retain original EdgeSyntax and ordered child builds.
Unions retain an actual indexed member. Variables retain their exact input
slot. Binders retain the selected stored Mu body and actual smart finish.
No source-binding ancestry or global decrease is assumed or inferred for
captured values or retained winners. These remain the next proof obligations.
